structure: Part 10: the animals accessibility suite. Read in full: the 12 spec files under tests/animals/a11y (notification-journey-initial-state, -filled-state, -error-state, -conditional-pages, -viewports, notification-dashboard-views, notification-dashboard-viewports, notification-view-states, notification-lifecycle-states, notification-address-edit, sign-in, a11y-scan-detects-violations), tests/animals/a11y/README.md, the a11y fixture (fixtures/a11y.ts), its helpers (utils/a11y-utils.ts, utils/a11y-exclusions.ts, utils/narrow-page-scan.ts), docs/a11y.md, the animals and shared page-object registries (page-objects/animals/index.ts, page-objects/shared/index.ts) and the animals journey flow (flows/animals/journey.ts, 1,095 lines) for the to* methods the a11y specs reach pages through. The 12 specs hold 16 literal test() declarations and run 18 tests, because notification-journey-viewports.spec.ts and notification-dashboard-viewports.spec.ts each loop one test over two narrow viewports. Every spec puts its tests in a describe titled `Accessibility ${WCAG_STANDARD.name}` tagged @a11y, and every scan goes through the runA11yScan fixture (except the scanner self-test, which calls scanPage directly). Laid out as: three specs that walk the whole live-animals journey once each and scan every page in one state (initial load, after user input, with validation errors shown); one spec for reason-gated and multi-species conditional pages; two specs that re-scan at 320x568 and 568x320; two for the live-animals notification list (default, sorted, 404, searched, paginated, and the list at both narrow viewports); one for the check-your-answers/notification view states; one for the cancel-amendment and delete lifecycle pages and their success banners; one for the copied-address edit page and the contact address page; one for the unauthorised sign-in error page from a cold start; and one that proves the scanner and the fixture fail a page that has a violation. Covered: every test by title, every page and state scanned, both narrow viewports with their sizes and stated reasons, the WCAG 2.2 AA tag set, the two conditional-reveal radio exclusions with the upstream reason given for them, the fixture's timeout, artefact and no-scan guards, and the pages the journey flow reaches that no scan covers (permanent address, four of the five party pickers, four of the five party edit pages, the contact address edit page, the sign-in and organisation-picker pages, and the INS add-address hand-off). The germinal-products set has no spec in this folder at all.

claims.statement: Every animals accessibility test is tagged @a11y, so the suite can be selected or excluded as a whole by tag.
claims.ref: tests/animals/a11y/notification-journey-initial-state.spec.ts:8 (and the same line in all 12 specs)
claims.quote: test.describe(`Accessibility ${WCAG_STANDARD.name}`, { tag: '@a11y' }, () => {

claims.statement: Every animals accessibility test is reported under the heading "Accessibility WCAG 2.2 AA", the standard being read from the fixture so the title and the rule set cannot drift apart.
claims.quote:
Couples the WCAG 2.2 AA name with axe's tags so describe titles and the
 * ruleset can't drift apart.

claims.statement: Accessibility scans are run against WCAG 2.2 AA, through the five axe tags wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21a, wcag21aa and wcag22aa, all five being needed for AA.
A clean scan is not full WCAG 2.2 AA conformance: axe automates only part of the standard, and of the criteria new in 2.2 it covers only 2.5.8 Target Size.
claims.quote: axe only automates part of the standard (only 2.5.8 Target Size among the new 2.2 criteria), so a pass isn't full conformance.

claims.statement: A scan always passes the WCAG tag set explicitly, because axe's own default rule set leaves target-size out.
claims.quote: // Without tags axe runs its own default ruleset, which omits target-size — see WCAG_STANDARD in @fixtures/a11y.

claims.statement: A scan waits for the DOM to be parsed, then allows up to the medium timeout for the network to go idle, and scans anyway when that wait times out.
claims.note: mechanism: settles the page before axe reads it; works on the Playwright page's load state, not on service data.

claims.statement: Each scan is recorded against the URL path of the page scanned, and a failing scan attaches its violations to the test result as JSON named "accessibility-violations: <path>".
A test that takes the scan fixture but never scans fails, rather than passing silently: "No accessibility scans were run. Call runA11yScan() at least once."
claims.quote: if (results.length === 0) throw new Error('No accessibility scans were run. Call runA11yScan() at least once.');

claims.statement: A test runs every one of its scans before failing, and reports them together as "Accessibility violations found on N pages", each page listed with its violations' severity, rule id, description, node count, help URL and first target.
claims.quote: const header = `Accessibility violations found on ${failed.length} page${failed.length === 1 ? '' : 's'}:\n\n`;

claims.statement: An accessibility test is allowed five minutes, because one test clicks through several pages and scans each of them.
claims.quote: const A11Y_SCAN_TIMEOUT_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000;

claims.statement: Scans run with axe's legacy mode off by default, and content inside cross-origin iframes is therefore scanned unless a scan opts into legacy mode to dodge an upstream hang in axe-core-npm's results window.
claims.quote:
Defaults to false — axe-core-npm opens a temporary blank window as part
   * of analyze() (since v4.3.0) to process results outside the page's
   * context, which is what allows testing content inside cross-origin
   * iframes, but that window-open can hang indefinitely under some
   * conditions
claims.note: No spec in this part passes legacyMode, so every animals a11y scan runs with it off.

claims.statement: A scan may be narrowed or widened per page through include, exclude and disableRules options, and the animals suite uses only exclude.
claims.note: Inferred: the option set is verbatim; that only exclude is used follows from every runA11yScan call in the 12 specs passing either nothing or an exclude selector.

claims.statement: The origin of import page's region-of-origin-code radio is left out of every scan of that page, by the selector #regionOfOriginCodeRequirement.
claims.quote: export const govukConditionalRevealRadioOnOrigin = '#regionOfOriginCodeRequirement';

claims.statement: The import reason page's radios that open a conditional reveal are left out of every scan of that page, by the selector input[name="reasonForImport"][aria-controls].
claims.quote: export const govukConditionalRevealRadiosOnReason = 'input[name="reasonForImport"][aria-controls]';

claims.statement: The exclusion is held to be an upstream disagreement between govuk-frontend's conditional-reveal radios, which set aria-expanded on the radio input, and axe's aria-allowed-attr rule, and not a defect in the service.
claims.quote: govuk-frontend's conditional-reveal radios set `aria-expanded` on the radio input in its `radios.mjs`, and axe's `aria-allowed-attr` rule rejects that. This is an upstream disagreement in component code the service does not own, not a defect in the service.
claims.note: The nearest thing to a ruling the a11y area records; the repo keeps no decisions ledger.

claims.statement: Only the inputs that carry the disputed attribute are excluded, never the page or a rule as a whole.
claims.quote: The scans exclude only the inputs that carry it, through the selectors in `utils/a11y-exclusions.ts`:

claims.statement: The import reason page offers five reasons, four of which open a conditional reveal, so four of its radios carry the disputed attribute.
claims.quote: | `conditionalReasonRadios` | Import reason    | Four of the five reasons open a conditional reveal, so four radios carry `aria-expanded`. |

claims.statement: The documented names of the two exclusion selectors, conditionalRadioInput and conditionalReasonRadios, no longer match the names the code exports, so the documentation table names selectors a reader cannot find.
claims.quote: | `conditionalRadioInput`   | Origin of import |
claims.note: Inferred from the two files side by side: the exports are govukConditionalRevealRadioOnOrigin and govukConditionalRevealRadiosOnReason.

claims.statement: Pages whose layout is re-checked for small screens are scanned again at 320 by 568 pixels, that being the WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow width (a 1280px desktop at 400% zoom) and govuk-frontend's smallest breakpoint.
claims.quote: narrowPortrait: { width: 320, height: 568 },

claims.statement: The same pages are scanned again at 568 by 320 pixels, the narrow viewport rotated, to catch layout that breaks on rotation (WCAG 1.3.4 Orientation) and the 256-pixel height half of WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow.
claims.quote: narrowLandscape: { width: 568, height: 320 },

claims.statement: A narrow-viewport scan also proves the page does not scroll sideways once its tables are discounted, reported as "<url> scrolls sideways"; a table is the only element allowed to scroll sideways at that width.
claims.quote: await expect.soft(scrollsSidewaysOutsideTables(page), `${page.url()} scrolls sideways`).resolves.toBe(false);
claims.note: mechanism: hides every table, measures document scrollWidth against clientWidth, then restores each table's display.

claims.statement: The suite's standing judgement is that not every reachable state earns its own scan: a state's value is weighed against the test infrastructure it needs, and states only reachable behind disproportionate set-up are skipped.
claims.quote: Not every reachable state is worth a dedicated scan — weigh the state's value against the test infrastructure it needs. Skip states that only exist behind disproportionate setup (e.g. seeding a real external queue to reach one rarely-used dialog).
